To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have demonstrated a new technique for measuring the scattering properties of milk components.
we are able, for the first time, to reconstruct the optical properties of milk components, by an iterative algorithm, based on the Gerchberg Saxton algorithm.
we have shown that the G–S algorithm is a robust tool to estimate the scattering coefficient of a given substance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of an innovative milk‐content‐measurement system based on the G–S iterative algorithm.
the development of a novel optical tool that is able to detect the presence of milk components, in particular lactose and milk protein.
the development and evaluation of a novel optical method for detecting concentrations of milk components.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we are able not only to detect the possibility, but also to quantify the concentration of the milk component by the proposed G–S algorithm.
the proposed method is capable of detecting concentrations of milk components.
the G–S algorithm is a powerful and robust technique for the reconstruction of the scattering coefficient of participating media.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that the optical tool, based on the iterative algorithm, can be applied in a practical way to reconstruct the reduced scattering coefficients for different milk components and concentrations.

the proposed G–S algorithm can be used to reconstruct the reduced scattering coefficient of a participating media, and that this coefficient is related to the standard deviation of the reconstructed phase.
the G–S algorithm can be used as an optical tool for the detection of concentrations of milk components.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the G–S algorithm can be used for detecting the concentrations of milk components, which can be used for the design of a new milk-content-monitoring tool.
the proposed method could be used for detecting the concentration of milk components by measuring the phase's STD of the remitted signal.
the G–S algorithm can be applied to reconstruct the optical properties of a given sample, and that the STD of the retrieved phase can be used to detect the presence of different milk components.
